title: leaving Vrindavan
carry: in the river, and in the chariot

segments.voice: Yesterday, leaving Vrindavan from the side of the ones who stay: the gopis in the road, a promise to come back, and the dust settling. Did you send that message to someone far away? Day nine hundred four.

On the road to Mathura, the chariot stops at the river. Akrura asks the boys to wait in the shade while he goes down to the Yamuna to bathe and say his prayers. He wades in, ducks under the water, and opens his eyes. Krishna and Balarama are there, under the river, looking at him. Which is strange, because he just left them sitting in the chariot. Today, the last of leaving Vrindavan: what Akrura sees in the water.
screen: `THE CHARIOT STOPS AT THE RIVER.` → `AKRURA DUCKS UNDER.` → `THE BOYS ARE IN THE WATER.`

segments.voice: Akrura does what anyone would do. He comes up for air and looks back at the bank. There's the chariot, and there are the two boys, sitting in it just as he left them. So he goes under again. And this time the vision is bigger. He sees Balarama as the great serpent Ananta, and resting on him, Vishnu himself, dark as a rain cloud, dressed in yellow, with sages and gods around him singing his praise. Akrura stays there in the river, and the Bhagavata gives him a long hymn of praise. Then he climbs out, dripping, and walks back to the chariot in a daze. Krishna looks at him and asks, kindly, whether he's seen something wonderful, in the earth or the sky or the water. And Akrura answers that every wonder in the earth, the sky and the water is in Krishna, and he's looking at him. So what does this scene do, here, on the road out of Vrindavan? The whole village has just watched Krishna leave. The gopis stood in the road until the dust was gone. And soon after, the text shows us a man discovering that the one he's driving to Mathura is also in the river, and also beyond all of it. The leaving is real; nobody in the story pretends it isn't. But the Bhagavata sets this vision right beside the grief, and some readers hear in it that the one who left the village hasn't left anything. Akrura gets back on the chariot, and they reach Mathura as the day ends. Krishna sends him on ahead, and walks into the city on foot, with the cowherds.
screen: `ON THE CHARIOT, AND IN THE RIVER.` · `VISHNU RESTING ON ANANTA.` · `EVERY WONDER IS IN YOU.` · then, large: `HE HASN'T LEFT ANYTHING.`

segments.voice: Sit, and close your eyes, the way Akrura closed them before he went under. Let the breath be slow, like water. Now open your inner eyes to something ordinary you will see again today: a kitchen, a street, a face. Look at it in your mind as if you'd just come up from the river and found it still there. Nothing needs to change. Just look twice. If you pray, you can ask to see God, or Krishna, in what is right in front of you. The bell holds the time.
Leaving Vrindavan. The journey to Mathura, where Akrura sees the boys on the chariot, and also in the river, and Vishnu beyond them.
Your line: in the river, and in the chariot. Today, before you decide you've seen all there is to something, go back and look again, the way Akrura went under twice. Day nine hundred four.

howItsDone: Akrura's hymn in the Bhagavata is recited by devotees, and pilgrims bathe at a place on the Yamuna that tradition links with his vision.

fork.setup: you're Akrura. under the river you see the two boys you just left in the chariot. you come up and they're still in the chariot. what do you do?
options: decide it was the light on the water.
go back under and look again.
hurry back to the chariot and say nothing.
fork.reveal: Akrura goes under again, and this time sees Vishnu resting on Ananta, and stays in the river singing praise.

original.note: Sanskrit and Hindi: Mathura, Kamsa's city on the Yamuna, where the chariot is headed.

trapdoor: what you thought: leaving Vrindavan is just a sad goodbye.
what it means: on the way out, Akrura finds Krishna on the chariot and in the river at once.
what a scholar hears: the Bhagavata sets this vision right after the gopis' grief, so separation and presence sit side by side.

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 10.39–10.41, Akrura's vision in the Yamuna, his hymn, and the arrival at Mathura

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm against Bhagavata 10.39 (roughly verses 40–57: midday stop at the Yamuna, the boys seen in the water and in the chariot, the second vision of Ananta and Vishnu), 10.40 (Akrura's hymn), and 10.41 (Krishna's question 'did you see something wonderful', Akrura's reply, arrival at Mathura in the late afternoon, Akrura sent ahead, entering on foot with the cowherds).
The interpretive line that 'the one who left the village hasn't left anything' is the script's framing, not a verse; a Keeper may want it attributed or softened.
howItsDone mentions a bathing place on the Yamuna linked with Akrura (Akrura Ghat); confirm or cut.
